newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 30.

text.p: The following are the top stories in the Irish press on Monday.
- Urgent talks between health insurance company BUPA Ireland and the Department of Health are continuing, to clarify the legality of some of BUPA's products.
- Sinn Fein has vehemently denied a newspaper report that Gerry Adams and Martin McGuinness have been appointed members of the Irish Republican Army's army council.

- Irish President Mary Robinson will announce early in 1997 whether she will run for a second term in office. - A particularly strong performance in the British and North American markets looks set to boost tourist earnings by 12 percent to 1.445 billion punts in 1996, the minister for tourism and trade said.
- Shannon Airport is overstaffed but no specific job cuts have yet been identified, a spokesman for Aer Rianta said.
- The three parties in Ireland's ruling coalition are gearing up to fight a May election on the strength of a budget which will combine tax cuts with social welfare increases.
- A 23-year-old Asian woman was found beaten to death in the bedroom of a Dublin apartment.
- 1997 will be another boom year for Irish exporters, according to the Irish Exporters Association.
- Bula Resources is set to announce a nine-million-punt exploration programme in Libya within the next three or four years.
